rationale: Boundary (unchanged ownership, current discovery fc9ec3b1, no bundles installed): the objective is generated exclusively by the 13 device NCCL kernels of DDP's synchronized final-micro-batch reducer - call d0938de87369efd500322679 (group f833b57a373d8262a384, 12 invocations x 7,087,872 fp32 elements = 28,351,488 B) and call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b (group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0, one 39,385,344-element = 157,541,376 B bucket) - both direct children of the single complete-workload project call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb); nsys-9ed9145c corroborates exactly 13 NCCL kernels and no other NCCL device work, and communication-ownership.json links the 13 buckets to member parameter groups without assigning each member group an independent communication cost (attribution_status joint_only). The scheduling lever must control dispatch of all three no_sync micro-batches plus the final synchronized micro-batch inside one invocation, so the whole project call is the coherent editable boundary; scope group with zero functional sites kept the effective binding 'direct' with 24.6-31.0 ms install and passthrough deltas +0.34/-4.78 ms (binding_cost-2087a4f7), whereas functional binding of the two allreduce_ sites under the fixed legacy backend measured +92.3/+100.8 ms clean step time and is evidence-barred, as are a pre-burst gloo barrier (trial-43f18a5360: rank-0 kernel sums 80.5/73.9/81.1 ms), communicator/NCCL-env rerouting (provider configuration; step constraint lost, 253.9-295.5 ms in trial-5a705e709d), precision/byte reduction (fails grad_atol=1e-6/grad_rtol=1e-4) and bucket fusion/comm hooks (preserved DDP configuration: bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, broadcast_buffers=False, no hook in the measured path). Concrete previous failure being repaired (previous-feedback.txt, trial-93aa5d5fc1, same boundary and plan): quality passed and the step constraint passed (139.51/143.73 vs limit 144.80), but the candidate was rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise (paired gains 0.41 vs 6.67 and 12.94 vs 5.65 ms MAD bounds) because the CUDA-graph path never executed - after the first parent-reference invocation, every invocation ran fallback:parent:capture_failed:RuntimeError on both ranks (candidate-declared routes, corroborated by candidate_diagnostics-2daf5302be exception evidence). The exact exception at the torch.cuda.graph capture of each no_sync segment (candidate.py line 254, called from line 347): 'During CUDA graph capture, autograd node torch::autograd::AccumulateGrad has a stale reference to the default stream (stream 0) from warmup. This will invalidate the capture because cudaStreamWaitEvent on the default stream pulls a non-capturing stream into the graph.' The measured paired gains were therefore parent-vs-parent noise; the replay policy itself remains unmeasured. The repair applies the error message's own documented fixes, verified present in the worker's measured environment (torch 2.13.0+cu129, /root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv/bin/python): (a) run the eager warmup of each segment on ONE explicit non-default stream S and pass that same stream to capture via torch.cuda.graph(graph, pool=pool, stream=S) so capture runs on the warmed stream, instead of warming on an unrelated side stream while torch.cuda.graph captures on its own internal stream; (c) enable torch.autograd.graph.set_override_stale_capture_stream(True) around the capture section to redirect the stale default-stream AccumulateGrad references (created by invocation-1's parent backward on stream 0) to the capturing stream, restoring the prior setting afterwards; and (b) drop the warmup loss/autograd-graph references before capture. Everything else keeps the previously validated design: explicit precomputed 4D causal mask (bypasses the earlier transformers 5.16.1 masking_utils.py:603 unpinned CPU-scalar capture killer; _preprocess_mask_arguments passes a prepared 4D mask through unchanged), bit-exactness re-verified on live inputs before any capture attempt, eager warmup outside capture surfacing lazy init, per-parameter primed in-place gradient buffers (about 497.8 MB), one graph per no_sync micro-batch in a shared pool replayed in capture order, static input buffers refreshed from current inputs each invocation, eager final micro-batch through the unmodified DDP reducer (all 13 bucket allreduces, their order and the reducer untouched), SGD step and the single final torch.cuda.synchronize, optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) inside the timed boundary, and permanent labeled parent fallbacks that never re-run the collective-bearing final micro-batch. Why the wait term is the recoverable slack (current observations, revision fc9ec3b1): execution_timeline-1221e205 shows rank 0 submitting every one of the 13 matched collectives 10.3-10.7 ms before rank 1 (cpu_submit_spread_bounds, matched cross-rank with anchor bounds), rank 0's first burst kernel running 14.058 ms vs 3.644 ms on rank 1 and rank 0's 13-kernel sum 74.379 ms vs rank 1's 63.985 ms under the perturbing hook; the separately warmed synthetic calibration at the exact observed sizes/dtypes gives intrinsic service floors of 3.536 ms per 28 MB bucket and 19.383 ms for the 157.5 MB bucket (61.82 ms rank-0 floor, 62.90 ms rank-1 floor at 8.0-8.13 GB/s logical payload over SHM/direct/direct, no P2P); clean diagnostic parent kernel sums were 63.21-66.48 ms (rank 0) and 63.41-64.12 ms (rank 1) in the original baseline and 68.83/77.26 ms at the last AB/BA parent endpoints. Kernel durations include device waiting by definition, so the difference between those sums and the warmed floor is arrival wait plus contention, not wire time; replay makes the CPU dispatch of the three unsynchronized no_sync micro-batches near-constant and early on both ranks, attacking exactly the accumulated submit spread that the earlier rank absorbs into its first kernel. Affected scope is exactly the selected group's call and its observed descendant closure (1525 calls, including the 13 allreduce-bearing calls d0938de87369efd500322679 and b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b); the two root-level opop phase-marker profiler calls (a60da373fdd5a4383277bf4e, ca1f233e0c891270f758ff58) sit outside that boundary closure and are excluded from affected_calls.
hypothesis: Testable hypothesis: the max-rank NCCL kernel sum for this step equals the warmed transfer floor plus a rank-arrival wait term, and that wait term is dominated by the 10.3-10.7 ms cross-rank CPU submit spread accumulated over the three unsynchronized no_sync micro-batches and absorbed into the earlier rank's first burst kernel. With the stale-stream capture failure repaired (warmup on the same explicit stream passed to torch.cuda.graph plus torch.autograd.graph.set_override_stale_capture_stream(True) around capture), the replay-only timed and profiled invocations dispatch the three no_sync micro-batches near-identically on both ranks, so both ranks enter the 13-kernel burst nearly aligned and the objective moves from the parent's observed 63.2-77.3 ms samples toward the ~61.8-62.9 ms calibrated floors - an expected paired gain of roughly 1-10 ms depending on which parent endpoint noise is drawn. To be measured, not assumed: acceptance requires every AB/BA pair to exceed its MAD-derived noise bound (6.67/5.65 ms last round), which the gain may not clear; clean step_ms must stay <= 144.80 ms (replay removes CPU dispatch work rather than adding it, and the failed-capture regime measured 139.5-143.7 ms, but capture must now actually succeed to matter); any residual capture hazard or replay-shape change must degrade permanently and safely to the parent reference with distinct labels, in which case this run acts only as a measured control; and the later rank's ~0.8-1.7 ms mid-burst excess above its floor may be transport jitter or SM contention that no in-contract scheduling change removes, pinning the in-contract floor. Fallback within the same boundary if alignment alone tests below the noise bound: tighten replay-side dispatch determinism (e.g. pre-refreshing static buffers before the burst), never touching DDP configuration, comm hooks, precision, buckets, the collective sequence, or the measurement boundary.
